advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the release step's `du`/`find` reporting non-fatal (or perform `rm -rf` before/independently of measurement) so a measurement failure cannot skip removal and leave the default tree for the integration tier.
evidence: Ticket comment: 'use a 2 GiB APFS volume, report and remove the exact successful default basetemp before integration ... keeps each tier's measured ~1.086 GiB peak below 2 GiB' — retaining both trees is 2.171 GiB, exceeding 2 GiB.
advisory.finding: In the release step, `du -sk` and `find ... | wc -l` run under `set -euo pipefail` and precede `rm -rf`, so a transient/permission failure of either measurement command aborts the step before the default basetemp is removed; the integration tier then reuses the same 2 GiB volume with the ~1.09 GiB default tree still present plus its own ~1.09 GiB, risking exhaustion of the bounded volume the ticket sizing (~87% headroom per tier, not both) relies on.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the reporting commands with `|| echo '::warning::...'`, or move the `rm -rf -- "$DEFAULT_BASETEMP"` so it executes regardless of whether du/find succeed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the final `hdiutil detach` a fallback (e.g. `|| hdiutil detach -force` and/or a `::error::` message) matching the setup-error path's resilience.
evidence: 638:             hdiutil detach "$device" || echo "::error::Failed to detach $device after setup error"
Ticket AC: 'Cleanup runs under always(), reports final filesystem usage, and detaches only the exact device'
advisory.finding: The final always-run detach `hdiutil detach "$RAMDISK_DEVICE"` has no failure fallback, unlike the setup-error path which uses `|| echo '::error::Failed to detach ...'`. If the volume is busy at detach time the always-run cleanup step fails hard with no diagnostic, and the RAM device may remain attached with no further cleanup attempt.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reduce test_ramdisk_setup_... to assert the observable contract (macOS-only guard, 2 GiB bound enforced, exact-device attach+detach, GITHUB_OUTPUT of device/mount_path) rather than pinning internal shell variable names and specific arithmetic/parameter-expansion forms.
evidence: These regexes pin internal variable names and the specific bash idiom used to compute sectors and strip the device token; renaming `sectors`/`device` or computing the sector count via a different equivalent expression is a behavior-preserving refactor that would fail these assertions.
advisory.finding: test_ramdisk_setup_is_macos_only_bounded_and_captures_exact_device asserts internal shell-script implementation detail (variable names captured via regex, the exact $((size / 512)) arithmetic form, and the ${var%%[[:space:]]*} parameter-expansion idiom) rather than observable routing/gating behavior; a behavior-preserving refactor of the setup script would break the test with no change in what the workflow does.
scenarios: A maintainer renames the internal `sectors`/`device` shell variables or rewrites the sector arithmetic equivalently; the RAM disk is still created identically but the test suite goes red.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the variable-name capture and arithmetic-form regexes; assert instead on stable observable tokens (e.g. presence of the 40%-of-hw.memsize refusal error string, `hdiutil attach -nomount ram://`, `diskutil erasevolume APFS RebarTests`, `echo "device=..." >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`, and the exact-device `hdiutil detach`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the du/find command-shape and index-ordering greps with the actual observable contract (exact default basetemp removed, integration basetemp untouched), dropping assertions on the specific reporting command names.
advisory.finding: The release and cleanup tests pin the presence and pre-removal ordering of internal diagnostic commands (du -s, find -type f) as reporting-shape assertions; these are internal implementation details of the diagnostic output, not an observable post-condition, and would break if the step reported usage a different equivalent way.
scenarios: The step is changed to report allocated usage/file count via an equivalent command (e.g. `du -sk` order changed, or usage reported from df output); the tree is still measured-then-released but the ordering/shape regexes fail.
